node-1.label: Patient had a 2-month history of an enlarging right anterior thigh subcutaneous mass

node-2.label: The lesion was asymptomatic but had grown significantly; the patient ran recreationally and recalled no trauma to the area

node-3.label: Physical examination revealed a 4-cm firm subcutaneous mass with no overlying epidermal change; the mass was palpable with right hip flexion and disappeared on right hip extension

why.why: Imaging shows no underlying mass, and dynamic maneuvers reproduce a mechanical fascial bulging rather than a fixed lesion. The absence of a detectable mass on ultrasound and MRI effectively excludes a soft tissue tumor, reducing confidence from 0.3 to 0.05.

Dynamic ultrasound and MRI demonstrate focal fascial bulging with rectus femoris convexity during hip flexion, absent on the asymptomatic side, and no underlying mass. These imaging findings directly confirm the clinical observation that the mass appears with hip flexion and disappears on extension, definitively supporting muscle hernia/fascial defect. Plain radiography is normal. Confidence is therefore raised from 0.6 to 0.95.

There is no overlying skin change, tenderness, or underlying mass on imaging, and dynamic ultrasound/MRI show a mechanical fascial defect rather than inflammatory or infectious changes. Normal radiography further supports the absence of an aggressive osseous or inflammatory process. Confidence is reduced from 0.1 to 0.02.

node-8.label: Plain radiography of the right thigh shows no osseous abnormality
